title: Never fabricate credentials or first-hand experience
statement: No page claims a qualification, a professional role, a test, a measurement, a visit, or any other first-hand experience that did not occur, and no such claim is introduced on behalf of the site by tooling.
rationale: A fabricated credential is a false statement about a real person or organisation that outlives the change which introduced it, and no later edit to the surrounding text removes the fact that the claim was published.
implementation: An automated agent must not write, expand, or embellish any statement of expertise, authorship, certification, or direct experience. Where a page would benefit from such context, report the gap and the specific claim that would be needed, and leave the writing to a person who can attest to it.

verification.method: A person with authority over the content reviews every added or altered claim of expertise or experience and confirms it is true before publication.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search, misleading functionality and scaled content abuse

title: Give each page one visible primary heading
statement: Each page renders exactly one top-level heading element, it is present in the response body, and its text names what the page is about rather than repeating the site name alone.
rationale: One top-level heading is what tells a reader arriving mid-document which page they are on, and a page with several competing top-level headings offers no single answer to that question.
implementation: Render the top-level heading from the layout or the page template, not from both, and demote any decorative use of the element in a banner or logo to a lower level or a non-heading element.

verification.method: Count the top-level heading elements in the served response for each sampled route and record the text of each one found.

caution: The specification permits more than one top-level heading in a document. Treating one as the target reflects widespread practice and the needs of assistive technology rather than a published requirement, which is why this record is tier B.

title: Keep critical information in crawlable text
statement: Facts a reader needs in order to act - price, availability, address, opening hours, contact route, key specification - appear as text in the response body rather than only inside an image, a canvas, a video, or a script-built widget.
rationale: Information that exists only as pixels or only after script execution is unavailable to anything reading the response, and the page then appears to omit the very fact it was written to convey.
implementation: Render the value as text next to or instead of the graphic that currently carries it. Where a widget owns the data, have the server emit the same values into the markup and let the widget enhance them rather than supply them.

verification.method: Search the unexecuted response body for each critical value the page displays and report values found only after script execution or only inside a media asset.

title: Structure body content with a nested heading outline
statement: Section headings descend one level at a time without skipping levels, and heading elements are used for section titles rather than for styling ordinary text.
rationale: The heading levels are the document's only machine-readable structure, so a skipped or misused level misstates which passages belong to which section for every consumer that relies on that structure to navigate.
implementation: Walk the rendered heading sequence and correct levels that jump by more than one, replacing style-driven heading choices with the correct level plus a class. In a component library, let the component take the level as a required input instead of hard-coding it.

verification.method: Extract the ordered heading levels from the served response and report every step that increases by more than one level.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.3.1 Info and Relationships

title: Publish dates that reflect real creation or revision
statement: A displayed or marked-up date corresponds to an actual publication or a substantive revision of the content, and no date is advanced by a build, a redeploy, a template change, or a trivial edit.
rationale: A date is a factual claim about when the content was written or changed, so refreshing it without changing the content misinforms readers and removes the site's own ability to tell which pages are genuinely stale.
implementation: Take the value from a content-modification field the editing system records, not from file modification time or build time. Where no such field exists, add one before displaying a date rather than substituting a proxy that a deployment can move.

verification.method: Redeploy without editing content and confirm the displayed and marked-up dates for unchanged pages are identical before and after.

title: Never generate keyword-stuffed or deceptive page text
statement: Text added to a page reads as prose written for a reader, without repeated keyword lists, hidden text, duplicated near-identical pages built from a template to catch query variants, or statements presented as facts that nothing supports.
rationale: Each of these patterns is named in published policy as a reason for demotion or removal, so producing them is not a neutral optimisation attempt but an action that can withdraw the site from the index.
implementation: An automated agent must not author body copy, headings, anchor text, or metadata whose purpose is keyword coverage rather than communication, and must not create near-duplicate pages differing only in a substituted term. Report the content gap instead of filling it.

verification.method: Inspect every text addition for repeated phrase density, off-screen positioning, and near-duplication against existing routes, and record each addition together with its purpose.
